title: Recording an outcome or deciding a rule drops keyboard focus to the page body
body:
## Summary
In Learning's Needs you queue, a successful Accept rule, Decline or Record removes the item's <li> on the refresh, and the button that held focus goes with it; focus falls to <body> and nothing is announced.

## Description
RuleOffer.decide (forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:206-207) and Candidate.record (:265-266) await the resolver, then onChanged = r.refresh (:133), which replaces reflect.data; NeedsYou keys items by id/ref, so the decided one unmounts with its focused button. No focus target is set and no success text exists (the only live text is the error SectionMessage). A keyboard or screen-reader user rating several accepted items must Tab from the top of the page after each one.

## Flow
- Tab to the first candidate, pick a rating, press Record
- Item disappears; document.activeElement is <body>
- Next Tab starts at the Jira chrome or page top, not the next candidate

## Expected impact
Rating a queue of outcomes by keyboard becomes one Tab per item instead of a hunt; screen readers hear 'Recorded' instead of silence.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - focus lands on the next item after a decision
Before: focus to <body>, no announcement
After: focus to the next item's first control (or the Needs you heading when empty) and a polite 'Recorded DW-n' status
Method: simulation - walked 3 cases (first of three, last item, rule offer) through reflect/index.jsx render keys; no browser in a read-only scout
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:206 `await call('rule.decide', payload);` :207 `await onChanged();` :265 `await call('outcome.record', payload);` :266 `await onChanged();` :133 `<NeedsYou d={d} projectKey={projectKey} onChanged={r.refresh} />` ; NeedsYou `{cands.map((c) => <li key={c.ref}><Candidate ...` - the decided ref is gone from the refreshed candidates
impact_why: The Learning queue is a repeated keyboard task; each decision loses the user's place

title: Use the rule.decide and outcome.record answers, not a reflect.data refetch
body:
## Summary
Both Learning writes already return what changed (the rule row; the outcome plus the new candidate list), yet the UI ignores the answer and reruns the whole reflect.data aggregate after every decision.

## Description
Contract: 'rule.decide' -> {rule: RuleRow}, 'outcome.record' -> {outcome, candidates} (forge/src/core/types.mjs:194-195; server forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:449 and :485 `candidates: await candidatesOf(...)`). The UI drops both results (forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:206, :265) and calls refresh (:207, :266 -> :34 fetchData(true)), i.e. a second invoke of reflect.data, which assembles totals, rejects, notes, pushes, lens_yield, rules, candidates, outcomes and trust (types.mjs ReflectData).

## Flow
- Record an outcome: invoke outcome.record (already computes candidatesOf)
- Then invoke reflect.data: recomputes candidates and every other section
- Per decision: 2 Forge invocations and 2 SQL fans

## Expected impact
Halves Forge invocations per Learning decision and removes the second round-trip latency before the item leaves.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - invocations per decision
Before: 2 invokes (write + reflect.data)
After: 1 invoke; patch d.rules / d.candidates / d.outcomes from the answer, keep a background refresh only for totals if wanted
Method: simulation - counted invoke calls per decision path in reflect/index.jsx against the contract; no Forge metrics reachable read-only
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/types.mjs:194 `'rule.decide': [..., {rule: RuleRow}]` :195 `'outcome.record': [..., {outcome: ..., candidates: OutcomeCandidate[]}]` ; forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:485 `return { outcome: ..., candidates: await candidatesOf(deps, item.project_key) };` ; forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:265 `await call('outcome.record', payload);` (result discarded) :266 `await onChanged();`
impact_why: Forge cost and latency on every Learning decision; the server already does the work

title: A failed silent refresh leaves a decided rule live, and the retry errors
body:
## Summary
After a successful rule.decide or outcome.record, a failed refresh is swallowed: the decided item stays on screen with its buttons enabled and no message, so the person presses again and gets 'rule ... is accepted, not offered; reload it'.

## Description
useReflect keeps the previous data when a silent fetch fails (forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:30). RuleOffer/Candidate treat the write as done and clear busy (:207-208, :266-267) with no confirmation. The stale item is indistinguishable from an undecided one. The server refuses a second decision on a decided rule (forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:445 `rule ${id} is ${now?.state ?? 'gone'}, not offered; reload it`), which the UI then shows as an error although the first decision succeeded.

## Flow
- Accept a rule: rule.decide succeeds
- reflect.data refresh fails (storage not ready, network)
- Rule still shows, Accept enabled, no message
- Press Accept again: red error 'rule X is accepted, not offered; reload it'

## Expected impact
The person sees that the decision landed even when the refresh did not; no false error.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a successful write is always acknowledged
Before: silent stale item + misleading error on retry
After: item removed from local state from the write's own answer (see the reflect.data refetch finding), refresh failure at most a quiet 'could not refresh' note
Method: simulation - walked success+refresh-fail, success+refresh-ok, write-fail through useReflect and RuleOffer; the fixture's &fail=reflect.data fails the first load too, so no probe isolates the refresh
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:30 `(error) => { if (mine === seq.current) setState((prev) => (silent && prev.status === 'ready' ? prev : { status: 'error', error })); },` ; :207 `await onChanged();` :208 `setBusy('');` ; forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:445 `throw new AppError('bad-input', `rule ${id} is ${now?.state ?? 'gone'}, not offered; reload it`);`
impact_why: False error after a successful decision erodes trust in the Learning loop

title: Lens direction limit errors name API keys, not the field labels
body:
## Summary
Settings > Lens direction labels its fields 'Focus on' and 'Leave out' and states the limits, but checks nothing client-side; the first a person hears of a limit is the server's message, phrased in API keys.

## Description
The hint promises 'One topic per line, up to 10, each up to 120 characters.' (forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:173) yet the Focus/Leave out textareas have no limit or count (:166, :170) and Save is enabled whenever dirty (:187). The server answers `focus holds 11 items; at most 10` or `each exclude item is one line of at most 120 characters` (forge/src/core/direction.mjs:36, :38), shown verbatim (:149, :192). 'exclude' appears nowhere on screen.

## Flow
- Paste 12 topics into Leave out, press Save
- Red text: 'exclude holds 12 items; at most 10'
- Person has to map 'exclude' to the 'Leave out' box

## Expected impact
Limit errors appear before Save, next to the right field, in the screen's own words.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - error names the field the person sees
Before: post-Save server message with API key names
After: inline count ('12 of 10 topics') per textarea, Save disabled while over; server message mapped to labels as a fallback
Method: simulation - three inputs walked (11 lines, a 130-char line, valid) through LensEditor and direction.mjs lines(); no running UI
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:173 `

One topic per line, up to 10, each up to 120 characters.

` ; :170 `
impact_why: Small, but it is the one place a team steers the scan in its own words

title: A saved Accept target missing from the project list shows as 'Choose a project'
body:
## Summary
When an inbox's saved jira_project_key is not among the projects jira.projects lists (project archived, renamed, or no longer visible to this person), the Settings row renders the placeholder and an empty issue type, so a configured target looks unset and its value is invisible.

## Description
InboxRow seeds `project` from the saved key (forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:203) and renders options only from `projects` (:234). A value with no matching <option> makes the select show its first option, 'Choose a project' (:233). Save stays disabled because nothing is dirty (:208, :245), and the saved key is shown only when the list is NOT loaded (:233 `saved.jira_project_key ?? 'Projects unavailable'`). Accept then fails at create time with Jira's error.

## Flow
- Inbox default target is BILL, later archived
- Settings lists projects without BILL
- Row shows 'Choose a project' / 'Choose an issue type'; no hint the default points at a gone project
- Accept fails in the dialog

## Expected impact
The admin sees the broken default where it is configured, before an Accept fails.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every saved target is visible
Before: saved-but-unlisted target renders as the placeholder
After: an extra option 'BILL (not available to you or archived)' selected, with a warning line
Method: simulation - walked listed, unlisted and unloaded cases through InboxRow; the fixture cannot list a project absent from PROJECTS without editing it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:203 `const [project, setProject] = useState(inbox.jira_project_key ?? '');` :233 `<option value="">{listed ? 'Choose a project' : loading ? 'Loading projects…' : (saved.jira_project_key ?? 'Projects unavailable')}</option>` :234 `{(projects ?? []).map((p) => <option key={p.key} value={p.key}>...` :208 `const dirty = project !== (saved.jira_project_key ?? '') || ...`
impact_why: A broken default is invisible exactly where it is fixed
